---
title: "Which function do I need?"
---

Each table lists tasks in the order a media mix or attribution project meets
them, with the function that does each one and, where it is the part that
does the job, the argument. `mm_weekly`, a simulated weekly media panel, and
`mm_events`, a simulated event log, are there to try each one on.

## Check the data

| Task | Function |
|---|---|
| Find channels that move together | `diagnose_media()`, its `collinearity` table |
| Measure that collinearity after adstock, as the model sees it | `diagnose_media()` with `decay` |
| Find channels that barely vary or are mostly dark | `diagnose_media()`, its `variation` table |
| Check spend against impressions for join errors | `diagnose_media()` with `spend` and `impressions`, its `cpm` table |
| Find missing, repeated or out-of-order weeks | `diagnose_media()` with `date`, its `dates` table |
| Check each geography on its own | `diagnose_media()` with `by` |
| Plot the checks | `plot()` on the result; see `plot.mm_diagnosis()` |

## Transform media

### Carryover

| Task | Function |
|---|---|
| Spread spend forward with a constant decay | `adstock_geometric()` |
| Let the effect peak a few periods after the spend | `adstock_delayed()` with `peak`, or `adstock_weibull()` with `type = "pdf"` |
| Use a Weibull kernel | `adstock_weibull()` |
| Apply a kernel you already have as weights | `adstock_filter()` with `weights` |
| Look at a kernel's weights | `adstock_weights()`, `adstock_weights_weibull()`, `adstock_weights_delayed()` |
| Turn a half-life into a decay, and back | `decay_from_half_life()`, `half_life()`; `period` converts between daily and weekly data |
| Decide how many lags a kernel needs | `effective_window()` |
| Keep the coefficient per unit of spend, or match Robyn's scale | `normalise = TRUE`, the default, or `normalise = FALSE` as in Robyn |
| Adstock several geographies at once | `by` in the adstock functions and in `media_transform()` |
| Treat missing spend as no spend | `na_action = "zero"` in the adstock functions, the default in `step_adstock()` |
| Continue a series from where an earlier chunk stopped | `adstock_state()`, passed as `state` |
| Remove the low first weeks of a long carryover | `adstock_steady_state()`, passed as `state` |

### Saturation

| Task | Function |
|---|---|
| Saturate with a Hill curve, concave or S-shaped | `saturate_hill()` with `half_max` and `shape` |
| Saturate with another curve | `saturate_exponential()`, `saturate_michaelis_menten()`, `saturate_power()`; `saturate()` picks one by `type` |

### Both, channel by channel

| Task | Function |
|---|---|
| Adstock then saturate one channel | `media_transform()` |
| Transform every channel of a data frame, each with its own parameters | `transform_plan()` with `spec` |
| Reproduce a Robyn model's transforms | `from_robyn()`, then `media_transform()` |
| Transform inside a tidymodels recipe | `step_adstock()`, then `step_saturation()` |
| Give each channel its own decay in a recipe | `step_adstock_channels()`, with `decay = c(tv = 0.85, search = 0.15)` |
| Keep the raw spend beside the adstocked column in a recipe | `step_adstock()` with `keep_original_cols = TRUE` |
| Start each series in a recipe at its steady state | `step_adstock()` with `start = "steady"` |

## Choose carryover

| Task | Function |
|---|---|
| Choose one channel's decay against the KPI | `tune_carryover()` |
| Choose every channel's decay inside one model | `tune_carryover_joint()` |
| Hold trend, price and seasonality fixed while choosing | `controls` in either tuner |
| Tune a panel of geographies | `by` and `index` in either tuner |
| Remove the start-up bias of long carryover while tuning | `warm_start = TRUE` |
| Take the shortest carryover the data cannot rule out | the `best_1se` element of the result |
| See how sharply the data identifies each decay | `plot()` on the result; see `plot.mm_carryover()` |
| Score candidates with your own model or metric | `fit_fn`, `predict_fn` and `metric_fn`; `rmse()` is the default metric and `mae()` the alternative supplied |
| Keep the out-of-sample forecasts | `save_pred = TRUE` |
| Tune carryover, saturation and a model penalty together | `step_adstock()` or `step_adstock_channels()` with `step_saturation()`, marked with `tune()` and searched by the tune package |
| Set the ranges a tidymodels search covers | `carryover_decay()`, `carryover_max_lag()`, `carryover_shape()`, `carryover_scale()`, `carryover_peak()`, `saturation_half_max()`, `saturation_shape()` |

## Add controls such as seasonality

| Task | Function |
|---|---|
| Model a smooth yearly cycle | `fourier_terms()` with `harmonics` |
| Flag the weeks that contain a holiday | `holiday_flags()`, with `align = "end"` for week-ending dates |
| Use them while choosing carryover | `controls` in `tune_carryover()` or `tune_carryover_joint()` |

For a trend, a column counting the weeks is enough.

## Fit a model

mediamix has no model of its own. The transformed columns are ordinary
numeric vectors, so `lm()`, `glmnet::glmnet()`, a brms or Stan model, or a
tidymodels workflow can take them. `fit_ols()`, a one-regressor least-squares
fit, is there as `tune_carryover()`'s default model.

## Report contributions and returns

| Task | Function |
|---|---|
| Split the model's predictions into channel contributions and a baseline | `contributions()` |
| Decompose a holdout or reporting period | `contributions()` with `newdata` |
| Decompose each geography | `contributions()` with `by` |
| Plot contributions over time, or in total | `plot()` on the result, with `type`; see `plot.mm_contributions()` |
| Average return per channel | `roi()` |
| Average return per geography or per year | `roi()` with `by`, or with `index` and `periods` |
| Return on the next unit of spend | `marginal_roi()` |
| Marginal return for every channel in one call | `marginal_roi()` on a data frame of spend, with `spec` |
| Count the carryover that falls after the last week | `marginal_roi()` with `extend` |
| Raise spend only in a planning window | `marginal_roi()` with `rows` |
| Slope of a saturation curve at one level | `mroi()` |
| A channel's response across spend levels | `response_curve()`; `plot.mm_response_curve()` shades the levels outside `observed` |
| Spend that reaches a target response | `spend_for()` |

## Measure uncertainty

| Task | Function |
|---|---|
| Intervals on coefficients, contributions or returns | `block_bootstrap()` |
| Choose how many weeks a resampled block holds | `block_length` in `block_bootstrap()`, at least the longest `effective_window()` |
| Resample a panel so shocks shared by every geography stay together | `by` in `block_bootstrap()`, with `panel = "shared"`, the default |
| Spread the replicates over several cores | `cores` in `block_bootstrap()` |
| Plot the intervals | `plot()` on the result, with `reference`; see `plot.mm_bootstrap()` |
| Intervals on attribution shares | `attribute()` with `times` |

## Plan budgets

| Task | Function |
|---|---|
| Predict each channel's response to a spend plan | `simulate_plan()` |
| Compare one plan with another | `simulate_plan()` with `baseline` |
| Move spend between two channels, keeping each one's flighting | `reallocate()` |
| Set up a move in one region only, as a geo test | `reallocate()` with `by`, and `amount` named by region |
| Split a total budget to maximise the predicted response | `allocate_budget()` with `total` |
| Keep each channel's spend within limits | `allocate_budget()` with `lower` and `upper` |
| Plot an allocation | `plot()` on the result; see `plot.mm_allocation()` |

## Build journeys

| Task | Function |
|---|---|
| Turn a raw event log into customer journeys | `build_paths()` |
| Start a new journey after each conversion or a quiet spell | `build_paths()` with `split_on` and `gap` |
| Drop touches older than a window | `build_paths()` with `lookback` |
| Choose that window from your own data | `conversion_lag()` |
| Keep, drop or relabel direct and missing channels | `build_paths()` with `direct` |
| Carry campaign, device or cost columns into the journeys | `build_paths()` with `keep` |
| Stop counting a checkout page as a touch | `build_paths()` with `conversion_touch = "drop"` |
| Read text timestamps in a format other than ISO 8601 | `build_paths()` with `timestamp_format` |
| Count events in, journeys out and conversions lost | `path_summary()` |
| Describe the journeys | `path_lengths()`, `channel_positions()`, `assisted_conversions()`, `top_paths()`; all of them at once with `path_diagnostics()` |
| Combine journeys built in separate batches | `bind_paths()` |
| Subset journeys and keep their touch ranks valid | `[` or dplyr verbs on the journey table; see [`[.mm_paths`](../reference/sub-.mm_paths.html) |

## Credit conversions

| Task | Function |
|---|---|
| Credit by a fixed rule | `credit_first()`, `credit_last()`, `credit_linear()`, `credit_position()`, `credit_time_decay()` |
| Credit by a rule of your own | `credit_custom()` with `fn` |
| Credit by Markov removal effects | `markov_removal()` |
| Inspect the fitted Markov chain | the `transitions` and `p_conversion` attributes of the result of `markov_removal()` |
| Run several rules side by side | `attribute()` with `rules` |
| See how much each channel's share depends on the rule | `attribution_spread()` |
| Credit each segment, such as device, separately | `attribute()` with `by` |
| Plot shares across rules | `plot()` on the result; see `plot.mm_attribution()` and `plot.mm_attribution_intervals()` |

## Export

| Task | Function |
|---|---|
| Hand journeys to ChannelAttribution for higher-order chains | `as_channel_paths()`, with the same `sep` on both sides |
| Get a tuner, diagnosis, bootstrap or allocation result as a plain table | `as.data.frame()` or `tidy()` on it |
| Read a recipe step's fitted state and parameters | `tidy()` on the prepared recipe |
| Match your own charts to the package's | `mm_palette()` |
